problem_description.description: Alice and Bob have decided to play the game "Rock, Paper, Scissors". The game consists of several rounds, each round is independent of each other. In each round, both players show one of the following things at the same time: rock, paper or scissors. If both players showed the same things then the round outcome is a draw. Otherwise, the following rules applied:  if one player showed rock and the other one showed scissors, then the player who showed rock is considered the winner and the other one is considered the loser;  if one player showed scissors and the other one showed paper, then the player who showed scissors is considered the winner and the other one is considered the loser;  if one player showed paper and the other one showed rock, then the player who showed paper is considered the winner and the other one is considered the loser. Alice and Bob decided to play exactly $$$n$$$ rounds of the game described above. Alice decided to show rock $$$a_1$$$ times, show scissors $$$a_2$$$ times and show paper $$$a_3$$$ times. Bob decided to show rock $$$b_1$$$ times, show scissors $$$b_2$$$ times and show paper $$$b_3$$$ times. Though, both Alice and Bob did not choose the sequence in which they show things. It is guaranteed that $$$a_1 + a_2 + a_3 = n$$$ and $$$b_1 + b_2 + b_3 = n$$$.Your task is to find two numbers:  the minimum number of round Alice can win;  the maximum number of rounds Alice can win.
problem_description.input_spec: The first line of the input contains one integer $$$n$$$ ($$$1 \le n \le 10^{9}$$$) — the number of rounds. The second line of the input contains three integers $$$a_1, a_2, a_3$$$ ($$$0 \le a_i \le n$$$) — the number of times Alice will show rock, scissors and paper, respectively. It is guaranteed that $$$a_1 + a_2 + a_3 = n$$$. The third line of the input contains three integers $$$b_1, b_2, b_3$$$ ($$$0 \le b_j \le n$$$) — the number of times Bob will show rock, scissors and paper, respectively. It is guaranteed that $$$b_1 + b_2 + b_3 = n$$$.
problem_description.output_spec: Print two integers: the minimum and the maximum number of rounds Alice can win.
problem_description.notes: NoteIn the first example, Alice will not win any rounds if she shows scissors and then paper and Bob shows rock and then scissors. In the best outcome, Alice will win one round if she shows paper and then scissors, and Bob shows rock and then scissors.In the second example, Alice will not win any rounds if Bob shows the same things as Alice each round.In the third example, Alice always shows paper and Bob always shows rock so Alice will win all three rounds anyway.

import heapq

class mcf_graph_int_cost:

    def __init__(self, n):
        self.n = n
        self.pos = []
        self.g = [[] for _ in range(n)]


    def add_edge(self, from_, to, cap, cost):
        # assert 0 <= from_ < self.n
        # assert 0 <= to < self.n
        m = len(self.pos)
        self.pos.append((from_, len(self.g[from_])))
        self.g[from_].append(self.__class__._edge(to, len(self.g[to]), cap, cost))
        self.g[to].append(self.__class__._edge(from_, len(self.g[from_]) - 1, 0, -cost))
        return m


    class edge:
        def __init__(self, from_, to, cap, flow, cost):
            self.from_ = from_
            self.to = to
            self.cap = cap
            self.flow = flow
            self.cost = cost


    def get_edge(self, i):
        _e = self.g[self.pos[i][0]][self.pos[i][1]]
        _re = self.g[_e.to][_e.rev]
        return self.__class__.edge(self.pos[i][0], _e.to, _e.cap + _re.cap, _re.cap, _e.cost)


    def edges(self):
        ret = []
        for i in range(len(self.pos)):
            _e = self.g[self.pos[i][0]][self.pos[i][1]]
            _re = self.g[_e.to][_e.rev]
            ret.append(self.__class__.edge(self.pos[i][0], _e.to, _e.cap + _re.cap, _re.cap, _e.cost))
        return ret


    def _dual_ref(self, s, t):
        self.dist = [4294967295] * self.n
        self.pv = [-1] * self.n
        self.pe = [-1] * self.n
        self.vis = [False] * self.n

        que = [s] # s ==  (0 << 32) + s 
        self.dist[s] = 0
        while que:
            v = heapq.heappop(que) & 4294967295
            if self.vis[v]:
                continue
            self.vis[v] = True
            if v == t:
                break
            for i in range(len(self.g[v])):
                e = self.g[v][i]
                if self.vis[e.to] or e.cap == 0:
                    continue
                cost = e.cost - self.dual[e.to] + self.dual[v]
                if self.dist[e.to] > self.dist[v] + cost:
                    self.dist[e.to] = self.dist[v] + cost
                    self.pv[e.to] = v
                    self.pe[e.to] = i
                    heapq.heappush(que, ((self.dist[e.to] << 32) + e.to))
        if not self.vis[t]:
            return False

        for v in range(self.n):
            if not self.vis[v]:
                continue
            self.dual[v] -= self.dist[t] - self.dist[v]
        
        return True


    def slope(self, s, t, flow_limit=4294967295):
        # assert 0 <= s < self.n
        # assert 0 <= t < self.n
        # assert s != t
        
        self.dual = [0] * self.n
        self.dist = [4294967295] * self.n
        self.pv = [-1] * self.n
        self.pe = [-1] * self.n
        self.vis = [False] * self.n
        
        flow = 0
        cost = 0
        prev_cost = -1
        result = [(flow, cost)]
        while flow < flow_limit:
            if not self._dual_ref(s, t):
                break
            c = flow_limit - flow
            v = t
            while v != s:
                c = min(c, self.g[self.pv[v]][self.pe[v]].cap)
                v = self.pv[v]
            v = t
            while v != s:
                e = self.g[self.pv[v]][self.pe[v]]
                e.cap -= c
                self.g[v][e.rev].cap += c
                v = self.pv[v]
            d = -self.dual[s]
            flow += c
            cost += c * d
            if prev_cost == d:
                result.pop()
            result.append((flow, cost))
            prev_cost = cost
        return result


    def flow(self, s, t, flow_limit=4294967295):
        return self.slope(s, t, flow_limit)[-1]

    
    class _edge:
        def __init__(self, to, rev, cap, cost):
            self.to = to
            self.rev = rev
            self.cap = cap
            self.cost = cost

import heapq

class MCFGraph:
    def __init__(self, n):
        self.n = n
        self.pos = []
        self.to = [[] for _ in range(n)]
        self.rev = [[] for _ in range(n)]
        self.cap = [[] for _ in range(n)]
        self.cost = [[] for _ in range(n)]

    def add_edge(self, fr, to, cap, cost):
        m = len(self.pos)
        self.pos.append((fr, len(self.to[fr])))
        self.to[fr].append(to)
        self.rev[fr].append(len(self.to[to]))
        self.cap[fr].append(cap)
        self.cost[fr].append(cost)
        self.to[to].append(fr)
        self.rev[to].append(len(self.to[fr]) - 1)
        self.cap[to].append(0)
        self.cost[to].append(-cost)
        return m

    class Edge:
        def __init__(self, fr, to, cap, flow, cost):
            self.fr = fr
            self.to = to
            self.cap = cap
            self.flow = flow
            self.cost = cost

    def get_edge(self, i):
        fr, idx = self.pos[i]
        to = self.to[fr][idx]
        rev_idx = self.rev[fr][idx]
        cap = self.cap[fr][idx]
        rev_cap = self.cap[to][rev_idx]
        cost = self.cost[fr][idx]
        return self.Edge(fr, to, cap + rev_cap, rev_cap, cost)

    def edges(self):
        res = []
        for i in range(len(self.pos)):
            fr, idx = self.pos[i]
            to = self.to[fr][idx]
            rev_idx = self.rev[fr][idx]
            cap = self.cap[fr][idx]
            rev_cap = self.cap[to][rev_idx]
            cost = self.cost[fr][idx]
            res.append(self.Edge(fr, to, cap + rev_cap, rev_cap, cost))
        return res

    def _dual_ref(self, s, t):
        INF = 10**18
        dist = [INF] * self.n
        pv = [-1] * self.n
        pe = [-1] * self.n
        vis = [False] * self.n
        dist[s] = 0
        pq = [(0, s)]
        while pq:
            d, v = heapq.heappop(pq)
            if vis[v]:
                continue
            vis[v] = True
            if v == t:
                break
            for i in range(len(self.to[v])):
                if vis[self.to[v][i]] or self.cap[v][i] == 0:
                    continue
                cost = self.cost[v][i] - self.dual[self.to[v][i]] + self.dual[v]
                nd = d + cost
                if dist[self.to[v][i]] > nd:
                    dist[self.to[v][i]] = nd
                    pv[self.to[v][i]] = v
                    pe[self.to[v][i]] = i
                    heapq.heappush(pq, (nd, self.to[v][i]))
        if not vis[t]:
            return False
        for v in range(self.n):
            if vis[v]:
                self.dual[v] -= dist[t] - dist[v]
        self.pv = pv
        self.pe = pe
        return True

    def slope(self, s, t, flow_limit=10**18):
        self.dual = [0] * self.n
        flow = 0
        cost = 0
        prev_cost = -1
        result = [(flow, cost)]
        while flow < flow_limit:
            if not self._dual_ref(s, t):
                break
            c = flow_limit - flow
            v = t
            while v != s:
                c = min(c, self.cap[self.pv[v]][self.pe[v]])
                v = self.pv[v]
            v = t
            while v != s:
                idx = self.pe[v]
                self.cap[self.pv[v]][idx] -= c
                rev_idx = self.rev[self.pv[v]][idx]
                self.cap[v][rev_idx] += c
                v = self.pv[v]
            d = -self.dual[s]
            flow += c
            cost += c * d
            if prev_cost == d:
                result.pop()
            result.append((flow, cost))
            prev_cost = d
        return result

    def flow(self, s, t, flow_limit=10**18):
        return self.slope(s, t, flow_limit)[-1]

import sys
import heapq

def solve():
    data = sys.stdin.buffer.read().split()
    it = iter(data)
    n = int(next(it))
    a1 = int(next(it)); a2 = int(next(it)); a3 = int(next(it))
    b1 = int(next(it)); b2 = int(next(it)); b3 = int(next(it))

    class Graph:
        def __init__(self, n):
            self.n = n
            self.pos = []
            self.g = [[] for _ in range(n)]

        def add_edge(self, fr, to, cap, cost):
            m = len(self.pos)
            self.pos.append((fr, len(self.g[fr])))
            self.g[fr].append(self._Edge(to, len(self.g[to]), cap, cost))
            self.g[to].append(self._Edge(fr, len(self.g[fr]) - 1, 0, -cost))
            return m

        class Edge:
            def __init__(self, fr, to, cap, flow, cost):
                self.fr = fr
                self.to = to
                self.cap = cap
                self.flow = flow
                self.cost = cost

        def get_edge(self, i):
            e = self.g[self.pos[i][0]][self.pos[i][1]]
            re = self.g[e.to][e.rev]
            return self.Edge(self.pos[i][0], e.to, e.cap + re.cap, re.cap, e.cost)

        def edges(self):
            res = []
            for i in range(len(self.pos)):
                e = self.g[self.pos[i][0]][self.pos[i][1]]
                re = self.g[e.to][e.rev]
                res.append(self.Edge(self.pos[i][0], e.to, e.cap + re.cap, re.cap, e.cost))
            return res

        def _dual_ref(self, s, t):
            INF = 10**18
            dist = [INF] * self.n
            pv = [-1] * self.n
            pe = [-1] * self.n
            vis = [False] * self.n
            dist[s] = 0
            pq = [(0, s)]
            while pq:
                d, v = heapq.heappop(pq)
                if vis[v]:
                    continue
                vis[v] = True
                if v == t:
                    break
                for i, e in enumerate(self.g[v]):
                    if vis[e.to] or e.cap == 0:
                        continue
                    cost = e.cost - self.dual[e.to] + self.dual[v]
                    nd = d + cost
                    if dist[e.to] > nd:
                        dist[e.to] = nd
                        pv[e.to] = v
                        pe[e.to] = i
                        heapq.heappush(pq, (nd, e.to))
            if not vis[t]:
                return False
            for v in range(self.n):
                if vis[v]:
                    self.dual[v] -= dist[t] - dist[v]
            self.pv = pv
            self.pe = pe
            return True

        def slope(self, s, t, flow_limit=10**18):
            self.dual = [0] * self.n
            flow = 0
            cost = 0
            prev_cost = -1
            result = [(flow, cost)]
            while flow < flow_limit:
                if not self._dual_ref(s, t):
                    break
                c = flow_limit - flow
                v = t
                while v != s:
                    c = min(c, self.g[self.pv[v]][self.pe[v]].cap)
                    v = self.pv[v]
                v = t
                while v != s:
                    e = self.g[self.pv[v]][self.pe[v]]
                    e.cap -= c
                    self.g[v][e.rev].cap += c
                    v = self.pv[v]
                d = -self.dual[s]
                flow += c
                cost += c * d
                if prev_cost == d:
                    result.pop()
                result.append((flow, cost))
                prev_cost = d
            return result

        def flow(self, s, t, flow_limit=10**18):
            return self.slope(s, t, flow_limit)[-1]

        class _Edge:
            def __init__(self, to, rev, cap, cost):
                self.to = to
                self.rev = rev
                self.cap = cap
                self.cost = cost

    INF = 10**9
    g = Graph(8)
    g.add_edge(0, 1, a1, 0)
    g.add_edge(0, 2, a2, 0)
    g.add_edge(0, 3, a3, 0)
    g.add_edge(4, 7, b1, 0)
    g.add_edge(5, 7, b2, 0)
    g.add_edge(6, 7, b3, 0)
    for i in range(1, 4):
        for j in range(4, 7):
            cost = 1 if (j - i) % 3 == 1 else 0
            g.add_edge(i, j, INF, cost)

    f, ans1 = g.flow(0, 7)
    ans2 = min(a1, b2) + min(a2, b3) + min(a3, b1)
    sys.stdout.write(f"{ans1} {ans2}")

        self.links[to].append([0, _from, len(self.links[_from]) - 1])

    def bfs(self, s):
        from collections import deque

        depth = [-1] * self.n
        depth[s] = 0
        q = deque([s])
        while q:
            v = q.popleft()
            for cap, to, _ in self.links[v]:
                if cap > 0 and depth[to] < 0:
                    depth[to] = depth[v] + 1
                    q.append(to)
        self.depth = depth

    def dfs(self, v, t, flow):
        if v == t:
            return flow
        links_v = self.links[v]
        for i in range(self.progress[v], len(links_v)):
            self.progress[v] = i
            cap, to, rev = link = links_v[i]
            if cap == 0 or self.depth[v] >= self.depth[to]:
                continue
            d = self.dfs(to, t, min(flow, cap))
            if d == 0:
                continue
            link[0] -= d
            self.links[to][rev][0] += d
            return d
        return 0

    def flow(self, s, t):
        INF = Dinic.INF
        flow = 0
        while True:
            self.bfs(s)
            if self.depth[t] < 0:
                return flow
            self.progress = [0] * self.n
            current_flow = self.dfs(s, t, INF)
            while current_flow > 0:
                flow += current_flow
                current_flow = self.dfs(s, t, INF)

    def get_edge(self, i):
        e = self.links[self.pos[i][0]][self.pos[i][1]]
        re = self.links[e[1]][e[2]]
        # from, to, cap, flow
        return (self.pos[i][0], e[1], e[0]+re[0], re[0])

    def get_edges(self):
        M = len(self.pos)
        res = []
        for i in range(M):
            res.append(self.get_edge(i))
        return res

import sys
from collections import deque

class Dinic:
    INF = 10**18

    def __init__(self, n):
        self.n = n
        self.head = [-1] * n
        self.to = []
        self.cap = []
        self.nxt = []
        self.level = [-1] * n
        self.it = self.head[:]

    def add_edge(self, fr, to, capacity):
        idx = len(self.to)

        self.to.append(to)
        self.cap.append(capacity)
        self.nxt.append(self.head[fr])
        self.head[fr] = idx

        self.to.append(fr)
        self.cap.append(0)
        self.nxt.append(self.head[to])
        self.head[to] = idx + 1

    def bfs(self, s):
        level = [-1] * self.n
        level[s] = 0
        q = deque([s])

        while q:
            v = q.popleft()
            e = self.head[v]
            while e != -1:
                if self.cap[e] > 0 and level[self.to[e]] < 0:
                    level[self.to[e]] = level[v] + 1
                    q.append(self.to[e])
                e = self.nxt[e]

        self.level = level

    def dfs(self, v, t, f):
        if v == t:
            return f

        e = self.it[v]
        while e != -1:
            if self.cap[e] > 0 and self.level[v] < self.level[self.to[e]]:
                d = self.dfs(self.to[e], t, min(f, self.cap[e]))
                if d > 0:
                    self.cap[e] -= d
                    self.cap[e ^ 1] += d
                    return d

            e = self.nxt[e]
            self.it[v] = e

        return 0

    def max_flow(self, s, t):
        ans = 0
        while True:
            self.bfs(s)
            if self.level[t] < 0:
                return ans

            self.it = self.head[:]
            while True:
                f = self.dfs(s, t, self.INF)
                if f == 0:
                    break
                ans += f

Find the number of ways to move the token from cell $$$n$$$ to cell $$$1$$$ using one or more shifts, and print it modulo $$$m$$$. Note that if there are several ways to move the token from one cell to another in one shift, all these ways are considered distinct (check example explanation for a better understanding).

The player is initially standing at the root of the tree and the exit from the tree is located at some leaf node. Let's index all the leaf nodes from the left to the right from 1 to 2h. Amr sequentially executes the characters of the string using following rules:  Character 'L' means "go to the left child of the current node";  Character 'R' means "go to the right child of the current node";  If the destination node is already visited, Amr skips current command, otherwise he moves to the destination node;  If Amr skipped two consecutive commands, he goes back to the parent of the current node before executing next command;  If he reached a leaf node that is not the exit, he returns to the parent of the current node;  If he reaches an exit, the game is finished. Now Amr wonders, if he follows this algorithm, how many nodes he is going to visit before reaching the exit?

BUFSIZE = 8192
class FastIO(IOBase):
    newlines = 0
    def __init__(self, file):
        self._fd = file.fileno()
        self.buffer = BytesIO()
        self.writable = "x" in file.mode or "r" not in file.mode
        self.write = self.buffer.write if self.writable else None
    def read(self):
        while True:
            b = os.read(self._fd, max(os.fstat(self._fd).st_size, BUFSIZE))
            if not b:
                break
            ptr = self.buffer.tell()
            self.buffer.seek(0, 2), self.buffer.write(b), self.buffer.seek(ptr)
        self.newlines = 0
        return self.buffer.read()
    def readline(self):
        while self.newlines == 0:
            b = os.read(self._fd, max(os.fstat(self._fd).st_size, BUFSIZE))
            self.newlines = b.count(b"\n") + (not b)
            ptr = self.buffer.tell()
            self.buffer.seek(0, 2), self.buffer.write(b), self.buffer.seek(ptr)
        self.newlines -= 1
        return self.buffer.readline()
    def flush(self):
        if self.writable:
            os.write(self._fd, self.buffer.getvalue())
            self.buffer.truncate(0), self.buffer.seek(0)
class IOWrapper(IOBase):
    def __init__(self, file):
        self.buffer = FastIO(file)
        self.flush = self.buffer.flush
        self.writable = self.buffer.writable
        self.write = lambda s: self.buffer.write(s.encode("ascii"))
        self.read = lambda: self.buffer.read().decode("ascii")

        # first 'at' at beginning: replace the next 'at' in the remainder
        rest = s[2:]

    if s and s[0] == '.':

n, m = map(int, input().split())
a = [int(x) for x in input().split()]
half = (n + 1) // 2
otv = 0

def build(start, cnt):
    sums = [0]
    upto = min(cnt, 20)
    for offset in range(upto):
        val = a[start + offset] % m
        sums += [(old + val) % m for old in sums]
    return sums

b = build(0, half)
b.sort()

for second in build(half, n // 2):
    target = m - second - 1
    k = bisect.bisect_left(b, target)

        if t2 > target and k - 1 >= 0:
            t2 = b[k - 1]
    else:
        t2 = b[-1]
    otv = max(otv, (second + t2) % m, (second + b[-1]) % m)

print(otv % m)

            P1[pos + 1] = (P1[pos] + pos * v) % mod

        lo = m - i * (i - 1) // 2

            R = t + rad

                rstart = L

import sys
sys.stderr = sys.stdout

def make_coeffs(n, mod):
    c = [0] * (n + 1)
    c[n] = 1
    k = n - 1
    while k >= 0:
        c[k] = (c[k + 1] * (k + 1)) % mod
        if c[k] == 0:
            break
        k -= 1
    return c

def build_all(n, mod):
    all_k = [[[1]]]
    i = 0
    while i < n - 1:
        old = all_k[i]
        width = i + 1
        nrows = len(old) + width
        new = [[0] * (width + 1) for _ in range(nrows)]
        j = 0
        while j < len(old):
            row = old[j]
            col = 0
            while col < len(row):
                value = row[col]
                h = 0
                while h < width:
                    new[j + h][col] += value
                    h += 1
                new[j + width][width] += value
                col += 1
            j += 1
        for r in range(nrows):
            for col in range(width + 1):
                new[r][col] %= mod
        all_k.append(new)
        i += 1
    return all_k

def contribution(rows, mod, coeff):
    R = len(rows)
    D = len(rows[0])
    pref = [[0] * D for _ in range(R)]
    j = 0
    while j < R:
        acc = 0
        col = D - 1
        while col >= 0:
            acc += rows[j][col]
            pref[j][col] = acc
            col -= 1
        j += 1
    j = 1
    while j < R:
        col = 0
        while col < D:
            pref[j][col] += pref[j - 1][col]
            col += 1
        j += 1
    for r in range(R):
        for col in range(D):
            pref[r][col] %= mod
    part = 0
    j = 1
    while j < R:
        col = 0
        while col < D - 1:
            part = (part + rows[j][col] * pref[j - 1][col + 1]) % mod
            col += 1
        j += 1
    return (part * coeff) % mod

def solve(n, mod):
    coeffs = make_coeffs(n, mod)
    tables = build_all(n, mod)
    ans = 0
    i = 1
    while i < n:
        ans = (ans + contribution(tables[i], mod, coeffs[i + 1])) % mod
        i += 1
    return ans

def main():
    n, m = map(int, input().split())
    print(solve(n, m))

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

We should remind you that a binary search tree is a binary tree, each node has a distinct key, for each node the following is true: the left sub-tree of a node contains only nodes with keys less than the node's key, the right sub-tree of a node contains only nodes with keys greater than the node's key. Bob gets the access to a Cube, when there are no trees left. He knows how many trees he will have to leap over in the worst case. And you?

def main():
    n, h = map(int, input().split())
    dp = [[0] * (n + 1) for _ in range(n + 1)]
    dp[0][0] = 1

    for nodes in range(1, n + 1):
        for height in range(1, n + 1):
            total = 0
            for left_nodes in range(1, nodes + 1):
                right_nodes = nodes - left_nodes
                total += dp[left_nodes - 1][height - 1] * sum(dp[right_nodes][i] for i in range(height))
                total += dp[right_nodes][height - 1] * sum(dp[left_nodes - 1][i] for i in range(height - 1))
            dp[nodes][height] = total

    print(sum(dp[n][i] for i in range(h, n + 1)))

main()

    cum_all = [dp[x][0] for x in range(n + 1)]
    cum_prev = [0] * (n + 1)

    for height in range(1, n + 1):
        cur = [0] * (n + 1)
        for nodes in range(1, n + 1):
            total = 0
            for m in range(1, nodes + 1):
                left_nodes = m - 1
                right_nodes = nodes - m
                total += dp[left_nodes][height - 1] * cum_all[right_nodes]

        old_all = cum_all
        cum_all = [old_all[x] + cur[x] for x in range(n + 1)]
        cum_prev = old_all

    print(sum(dp[n][i] for i in range(h, n + 1)))

dp = [ [-1]*(n+1) for i in xrange(n+1)]

dp[0][0] = 1
def f(n, h):
    if dp[n][h] != -1:
        return dp[n][h]

    if n == 0:
        return 0
    if h == 0:
        return f(n, 1)

    ans = 0
    for i in xrange(n): #0 .. n-1
        ans += f(n-i-1, 0) * f(i, h-1)
        ans += f(n-i-1, h-1) * f(i, 0)
        ans -= f(n-i-1, h-1) * f(i, h-1)

    dp[n][h] = ans
    return ans
